messages:
maria: Hey team — we just started getting 401 invalid_api_key on our service integration. This was working this morning. No code changes deployed. Error from our app: "{"error":"invalid_api_key"}". Can someone help?

jamie: Hi Maria — can you paste the exact Authorization header (sanitise please) and a curl repro?

maria: Sure. Here's the header and curl we used (sanitised):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key svc_AbC123xYz==" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

jamie: Thanks. Two quick checks: 1) Confirm this key came from your SCIM/service-account provisioning? 2) Can you try the raw token without any prefix (i.e., remove the leading `svc_` if present) and paste just the first/last 6 chars so we can match?

maria: Yes SCIM created it via our IdP (okta) yesterday. If I try without the prefix I get the same error. First/last 6: `AbC123...xYz==`.

jamie: Ok. Pinging scim-bot to see the provisioned value. @scim-bot can you dump the token metadata for maria-team-service? (only metadata, do not print the secret) :eyes:

scim-bot: Created service token for user maria-team-service at 2026-03-10T09:12:11Z. Token label: `svc_maria-team`. Token value stored as base64 string (masked in logs). No expiry set.

alex: Quick theory — our SCIM integration used a label prefix `svc_` that was included in the user-visible string. The actual secret stored in our vault does NOT include the `svc_` prefix, but the SCIM payload accidentally concatenated label+secret into the display value that the IdP showed. If the client copies the full display value including `svc_`, the server rejects it.

maria: Ohhh that would explain it — the IdP UI showed `svc_AbC123xYz==` and the engineer copied it whole. Any way to confirm?

jamie: I can confirm from server-side lookup — the token in our vault is `AbC123xYz==` (matches the start/end you shared). The incoming header from your app had `svc_AbC123xYz==` so it didn't match the stored secret. We return generic 401 for security.

dev-ops: Thanks for the repro. Maria, can you try a curl with the trimmed token?

maria: Trying now...

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Api-Key AbC123xYz==" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

maria: Works now, 200 returned. Thanks! :tada:

jamie: Root cause: SCIM provisioning returned a user-facing string that combined label+secret. Action items: 1) We'll patch SCIM mapping so the IdP display value is only the label (no secret). 2) We'll add a server-side len/format check to give a clearer error (currently generic 401). 3) We'll send an email to affected customers about service-token formatting.

alex: I filed an internal task (ENG-4278) to update the SCIM mapping and add a small validation on token ingestion.

maria: Appreciate the quick help. One request — can you add a short note in the docs about token formats (label vs secret) so our SREs don't copy the label+secret in future?

jamie: Yep, we'll add a doc blurb and include a small screenshot of the IdP UI to show where the secret lives. I'll also attach the support ticket: #SUP-33210.

scim-bot: Support ticket created: SUP-33210 (assigned to jamie).

maria: Thanks everyone. Closing from our side once docs are live.
